article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: The morning board kept the Bears on two cards and the Bills on one, Chicago's quarterback decision rolls into Wednesday's practice, and Thursday night in Cleveland gets a weather watch.

items.headline: Morning board: the Bears hold two cards, and the Value read got warmer
paragraphs: The 6 a.m. refresh is in, and the shape is the same as last night: Hit Rate on Bills moneyline (-290 at DraftKings; the app gives Buffalo a 71.2% chance to win, MEDIUM reliability), Balanced and Value both on Bears -3.5 (-102 at both books; the app's cover probability 50.5%, MEDIUM reliability).
The one overnight change is in the Value card's read: the expected return on Chicago -3.5 climbed from +0.6% last night to +2.7% this morning — same line, warmer read.
items.takeaway: Bears -3.5 carries two cards this morning; the Value read strengthened overnight.

items.headline: Still no Bears quarterback announcement
paragraphs: Ben Johnson stayed non-committal on the Week 4 starter: "We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here" — but reminded everyone that "there was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."

The app still projects Tyson Bagent, which matches where the winds are leaning. Case Keenum started Monday's 27-7 win over Philadelphia; Caleb Williams' Grade 2 hamstring strain is a three-to-four-week absence (Adam Schefter).

If Johnson names a starter at Wednesday's practice, the app's number was priced for the other guy. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app re-runs the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

items.takeaway: No Bears QB announcement yet; the app projects Bagent. A Wednesday announcement makes Check the move.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Washington: Jayden Daniels practiced in some form and flew with the team to London, but he's still unlikely to play Sunday — Marcus Mariota is expected to start against Indianapolis (London, 7:30 a.m. Denver kickoff). RG Sam Cosmi (concussion) and S Nick Cross (illness) didn't make the trip and are ruled out. Frankie Luvu (groin) and Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) traveled and could practice.
Tampa Bay: Baker Mayfield's dislocated throwing thumb costs him at least three weeks; undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starts — which is what the app already reflects. Green Bay is -3.5 at Tampa.

Elsewhere: Miami's De'Von Achane tore his ACL and is done for the season. The Jets' Breece Hall is week-to-week (quad). New Orleans' Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) won't play in Week 4. Day-to-day: Mike Evans (rib), Justin Jefferson (ankle).

Commanders Wire: Cosmi, Cross ruled out for London

items.takeaway: Mariota expected again for Washington; Tampa rolls with Jalon Daniels; Achane done for the year.

items.headline: Weather: Thursday night in Cleveland is watchable, for now
paragraphs: NWS hourly for the Steelers-Browns kickoff (8:15 p.m. ET): around 75 degrees, mostly cloudy, a slight chance of rain showers — about a 1-in-4 chance — with light southerly wind near 7 mph.

Rain showers get more likely later overnight (80% chance over the night window, per the daily forecast), so the wet part may arrive after the final whistle. Sunday's kickoff windows are still five days out; those forecasts get real Thursday or Friday.
items.takeaway: Cleveland Thursday: ~75°F at kickoff, slight shower chance, light wind. Sunday windows firm up Thu/Fri.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: When two cards agree, the app is saying the same thing two ways
paragraphs: Balanced and Value both landed on Bears -3.5 at -102. Balanced is the app's "strong pick without paying too much" — its starting point for a newer bettor. Value is always the model's +EV play. When the middle-ground pick and the +EV pick are the same ticket, two different grading systems arrived at the same answer.

Read the price tag: the app's fair price for this play is -105. You can buy it at -102 — three cents better than fair. That gap is what a +2.7% edge looks like: a small price difference, not a hunch. The book's -102 says Chicago needs to cover just over half the time to break even; the app's number lands a shade above that.
The reason, not the guarantee: the app expects Chicago to win by about 5.7 points on the field against a -3.5 line — a little over two points of cushion between the forecast and the number.
items.takeaway: Two cards, one Bears play. -102 is three cents better than the app's -105 fair price.

items.headline: Read the Hit Rate card for what it is
paragraphs: Bills moneyline -290, and the app gives Buffalo a 71.2% chance to win. The Hit Rate card answers one question: which supported pick looks most likely to win. The app's own tutorial says it plainly — Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. That's a description of the card's job, not a knock on it.
Read the overnight price move as a price tag: -298 last night, -290 this morning. Buffalo got a few cents cheaper. That's the market nudging the sticker price, not a verdict on the Bills.

Price mechanics: -290 means every $2.90 you risk wins $1. And the app sets your stake from your bankroll plus a deliberately conservative aggressiveness — for the actual number, look at the app, not this page.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Bills got a few cents cheaper overnight; the app sets your stake.

items.headline: Bills moneyline: -298 to -290 overnight
paragraphs: Between the 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. boards, Buffalo's moneyline price eased from -298 to -290 on DraftKings while the app held the Bills at a 71.2% win chance. The morning board caught the move — it was already at -290 by 6:08 a.m.

If your book shows anything off -290, this is the textbook Check moment: type in your number and the app re-runs the model and the evaluator on YOUR price and returns a bet/no-bet verdict. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Bills drifted a few cents cheaper overnight; the morning board has it. Check any price that isn't the board's.

items.headline: Bears -3.5: steady on both books, warmer read
paragraphs: Chicago -3.5 sat at -102 on DraftKings and FanDuel through the whole evening-to-morning window — no movement. But the Value edge went from +0.6% to +2.7% on the same line. Lines sleep; the app's read doesn't have to.
Giants +1.5 (-110) and Packers -3.5 (-120) also held overnight. The Giants edge that died last night stays dead.
items.takeaway: No line movement on the Bears — but the Value read warmed from +0.6% to +2.7% on the same -102.

items.headline: Wednesday is practice-report day — Thursday game gets a Thursday check
paragraphs: Week 4's first full practice day is today. Watch whether Bagent takes first-team reps (or Johnson finally names a guy) and whether Daniels practices fully in London. Thursday's inactives post about 90 minutes before the Steelers-Browns kickoff at 6:15 p.m. Denver.
Thursday game? Thursday check. And the recurring honesty nudge: settlement is manual, no auto-settle — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: lay
paragraphs: When you bet a favorite, you "lay" the points or the price — you give the spread. Taking the Bills moneyline at -290 means laying -290: you risk the bigger number to win the smaller one. Taking Chicago -3.5 means laying 3.5 points: the Bears have to win by more than a field goal.
items.takeaway: Lay = bet a favorite, giving the points or the price.
